title.narrative: Second Greater Mekong Subregion Corridor Towns Development Project

description.narrative: The Second Greater Mekong Subregion (GMS) Corridor Towns Development Project (the project) represents the second phase of the ongoing GMS Corridor Towns Development Project in Cambodia, Lao PDR and Viet Nam. It supports the first four strategic thrusts of the GMS Strategic Framework 2012-2022 namely (i) strengthening infrastructure linkages; (ii) facilitating cross-border trade, investment, and tourism; (iii) enhancing private sector participation and competitiveness; and (iv) developing human resources. The focus on corridor town development follows an approach that will maximize the economic benefits of increased trade and traffic flows along the major transport corridors in the GMS with the expected positive impacts resulting from accelerated investments in strategically located towns and cities, and added value on economic growth through development oriented on green growth and climate resilience. The objective is to strengthen competitiveness of the GMS economic corridors through environmental infrastructure.

description.narrative: 5,800 households (25,000 people, of whom 50% are female) serviced by improved solid waste collection Achievement: 6820 Progress/Status: 6,820 households (34,325 people, of which 17,849 (52%) are females will benefit from the improved service. Data Source: PDPWT reports, project progress reports, and end-of-project survey

At least 1,400 households (6,000 people, of whom 50% are female) benefit from reduced flooding Achievement: 2890 Progress/Status: 2,890 households (20,129 people, of which, 7,778 (52%) are females) will benefit from reduced flooding in five communes. Data Source: PDPWT reports, project progress reports, and end-of-project survey

At least 2,400 households (10,000 people, of whom 50% are female) serviced by a new wastewater collection and treatment facility Achievement: 3789 Progress/Status: 3,789 households consisting of 14,835 people of which 7,778 =52% are females will benefit from the new wastewater collection and treatment facility. Data Source: PDPWT reports, project progress reports; end of project survey.

Output: Institutional capacities for managing public investments strengthened Indicator: At least 100 community leaders, government officers, and consultants involved in project implementation and delivery demonstrate improved knowledge of gender-sensitive approaches because of training received (with 50 female participation) Progress/Status: 286 (75=26% female) persons consisting of community leaders, government officers and consultants participated in gender sensitization and project awareness campaigns. Data Source: Project progress and completion reports, attendance lists, and training reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacities for managing public investments strengthened Indicator: At least 20 persons from the project management unit and project implementation unit (30% female) are trained in project management Achievement: 20 Progress/Status: There were 13 people (4 PMU, 9 PIU) from PMU and PIU trained, out of 13 only 4 females (31%) participated (1 PMU and 3 PIU). Data Source: Project progress and completion reports, attendance lists, and training reports

Output: Priority urban infrastructure investments implemented Indicator: New managed landfill made operational Progress/Status: Construction completed. Handover on 30 May 2023. Establishment of the SWM O&M unit already done. Data Source: Construction records, progress monitoring reports, and project completion reports Actual value:

Output: Priority urban infrastructure investments implemented Indicator: Subproject construction, and operation and maintenance activities will support equal employment, including at least 30% female staff Progress/Status: Total of 1,252 (436=35% females) workers were employed. For O&M, the project's O&M manuals specify the employment of the required % of women workers. - Type of activities performance by women included: (i) bending bar, and casting cover rebar of concrete Female unskilled workers received training from the company on concrete work, rebar work, and bending, installing rebar to enable their work in the construction. Women unskilled laborers receive from $8.00 - $8.75/day. The company provide equal pay for equal work Data Source: Contractor's records and progress monitoring reports Actual value:

Output: Priority urban infrastructure investments implemented Indicator: Subproject construction, and operation and maintenance employment for unskilled staff and laborers will include at least 75% local hires Progress/Status: 2,509 (100%) local hires were employed. For O&M, the project's O&M manuals specify the employment of the required % of local hires. Data Source: Contractor's records and progress monitoring reports Actual value:

Output: Priority urban infrastructure investments implemented Indicator: Wastewater treatment plant with a capacity of 3,300 m3/day constructed and operational Progress/Status: Construction completed on 8 September 2023. Handover on 15 December 2023. Capacity of WWTP is 3300 m3/day. WWTP was tested by last ADB mission and is operational. Data Source: Construction records, progress monitoring reports, and project completion reports Actual value:

Output: Priority urban infrastructure investments implemented Indicator: Continued access to existing dump sites secured alongside livelihood skills training activities for at least 80% of informal waste pickers, of whom 65% are female Progress/Status: The training on Livelihood Improvement to waste pickers engaged 87 (65 = 74% females) waste pickers and 21 (2 females) PIUs and local authorities, in total they were 108 participants. Participants found the training very useful as they aware better about the sanitation as it can maintain of good health and how to do the compost (fertilizer) and important of recycling that can make more money in term of selling it to the dealer. The assessment done by gender specialist in April 2023: there are 54 (10 FHHs) full time waste pickers which consist of 238 (122 = 51% are females) while baseline figure in 2019 stated there were 35 HHs (22 FHHs) full time waste picker; part-time waste picker is 10 HHs (5 FHHs). Data Source: Construction records, progress monitoring reports, and project completion reports Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2023 Target value: Y
